Elon Musk says SpaceX (SPCX) will likely top $500 billion in ARR by December 2027, roughly triple the $180 billion analyst consensus.

SpaceX's third quarter annualizes to $58 billion, so Musk's target demands about 8.6 times that level in roughly 14 months.

Rocket Lab (RKLB) and AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) carry market caps of $31 billion and $10 billion, dwarfed by SpaceX's $1.76 trillion valuation.

Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

Elon Musk just put a number on SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) that sits above every revenue model on Wall Street. He spoke at the Baron Investment Conference, and Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) and SpaceX watcher Sawyer Merritt relayed the remark on X:

24/7 Wall St.

"It seems quite likely that our ARR in Dec 2027 will exceed $500B. This is not a promise, this is my best guess. $1 trillion..."

Merritt's summary added that $1 trillion is "not out of the question" and said Musk had "reiterated" the view.

Musk's Floor Clears Even the Most Bullish Analyst

Thirty-seven analysts put average fiscal 2027 revenue at roughly $180 billion. The high estimate is $290 billion and the low is about $72 billion. Musk's floor comes to about 2.8 times consensus and sits roughly $210 billion above the Street's most aggressive model.

ARR, or annual recurring revenue, usually takes one month of recurring sales and multiplies it by 12. Analysts model total revenue for the full year. A company that reaches a $500 billion run rate in December would book much less than that across the whole year, so the two figures don't line up exactly. Musk did not define the term, and he presented the figure as his best guess.

That quarter annualizes to $58.4 billion, and Musk's target is about 8.6 times that level, roughly 14 months out.

title: 4 Stocks I'm Not Selling Even If the Fed Keeps Raising Rates

4 Stocks I'm Not Selling Even If the Fed Keeps Raising Rates
Prosper Junior Bakiny, The Motley Fool

The Federal Reserve raised interest rates in September, and another hike is widely expected by the end of the year. The relationship between higher interest rates and stock market returns is complicated, but because higher rates raise the cost of borrowing, they can put downward pressure on equity markets as investors brace for lower corporate earnings.

This is certainly a meaningful risk worth monitoring, but there are plenty of stocks that could perform well over the long run regardless of whether the Fed raises interest rates again soon. Four of my holdings fit the bill, in my view, and I intend to keep all four intact well beyond the next interest rate increase. Here are these four stocks: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), Walmart (NASDAQ: WMT), and Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRKA) (NYSE: BRKB).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.
1. Johnson & Johnson

Johnson & Johnson's business is relatively insensitive to interest rate hikes, a tool the Federal Reserve uses to slow spending and economic activity and rein in inflation. This can lead to lower demand for many products and services, but not for the kind that Johnson & Johnson offers. The pharmaceutical giant boasts a deep pipeline of lifesaving drugs, which should remain in high demand regardless of economic conditions. Johnson & Johnson's medical device business is also fairly resilient. And on top of that, Johnson & Johnson boasts a rock-solid balance sheet.

Perhaps the best evidence for that claim is the company's AAA rating -- the highest rating possible -- from S&P Global. Of course, none of that guarantees that Johnson & Johnson will perform well over the next year. But the company's business is well-equipped to navigate a high-interest rate environment and continue performing well long after, as it expands its product lineup through innovation. Finally, Johnson & Johnson is a fantastic income stock. It has increased its dividends for 64 consecutive years, making it a Dividend King, or a stock with at least 50 straight annual payout hikes.

2. Amazon

Amazon has a vast business that spans e-commerce, cloud computing, advertising, video and music streaming, and more. Some of the company's segments could experience lower demand if interest rates continue to rise. For instance, corporations may reduce their advertising budgets and demand fewer cloud services as customers cut retail spending. This may lead to lower revenue and earnings than the tech leader would otherwise generate. But I'd stick with Amazon through thick and thin. Here's why.

Although Wall Street enjoyed more than nine months of a steady Federal Reserve, with the target rate capped at 3.75% from December 11, 2025 through September 16, 2026, that calm ended when policymakers lifted the ceiling to 4.00%, where it has sat since September 17. The quarter-point move ended the pause. But prediction markets expect more. On Kalshi, the contract for a 25-basis-point hike at the December 9 meeting last traded at $0.70, meaning roughly 70% odds, while a hold traded at $0.33. One sector to examine as borrowing costs climb: consumer staples.

Courtesy of Walmart Corporate Media / corporate.walmart.com
Why Essentials Hold Up When Money Gets Expensive

Staples sell what households replace on a schedule: detergent, diapers, soda and groceries. When higher rates squeeze budgets and slow the economy, shoppers put off a new couch long before they skip toothpaste. Strong brands can raise prices to offset rising costs while keeping most customers, and discount retailers scoop up trade-down traffic from shoppers hunting for value.

Best Buy (BBY) raised its dividend just 1% in 2026, down from raises above 25% in 2021 and 2022, as cash flow shrank.

Target (TGT) and Walmart (WMT) are raising dividends faster, while Best Buy offers a 4% yield in exchange for slower growth.

Dividends consume about 64% of free cash flow, so the payout looks safe even though raises have stalled.

Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

Best Buy (NYSE:BBY) has become a high-yield retailer with almost no dividend growth. The quarterly payout is $0.96, and it reached that level through a 1.1% raise in 2026, the same size as the 1.1% raise in 2025. Best Buy usually declares its December-quarter dividend with its fiscal third-quarter results. Last year that came on Nov 25, 2025. That makes the upcoming report the next dividend decision point.

Justin Sullivan / Getty Images News via Getty Images
BBY Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.
From 27% Raises to Token Bumps

Best Buy raised its quarterly rate by 27.3% in 2021 and 25.7% in 2022. Growth then fell to 4.5% in 2023 and 2.2% in 2024. Cash flow explains most of the slowdown. In fiscal 2022, operating cash flow was $3.252 billion and net income was $2.454 billion. By fiscal 2026, those figures had fallen to $1.962 billion and $1.069 billion. Over the same stretch, annual dividend spending rose from $688 million to $801 million. The board kept paying more while the company earned less, so it held back on raises.

title: Walmart expands drone delivery with 300 Zipline locations
detail:
Walmart expands drone delivery with 300 Zipline locations
The aerial service is part of Walmart’s wider same-day fulfilment options. Credit: Walmart. · Retail Insight Network · Walmart.
Shubhendu Vimal
Fri, November 6, 2026 at 3:01 AM MST 2 min read
WMT
ZIPL.PVT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart has agreed to a multi-year partnership with drone delivery company Zipline to add 300 delivery locations across the US, widening its national drone logistics operation.

The deployment builds upon an existing programme between the retailer and Zipline that commenced in 2021.

Walmart stated that its drone delivery scheme has so far completed more than two million deliveries.

Where available, the service delivers eligible products in as fast as 30 minutes.

Customers within the designated service radius can select drone fulfilment via the Walmart website or mobile application, or place qualifying orders through the Zipline app.

Drops are made directly to front gardens, back gardens, or driveways, with Zipline aircraft remaining approximately 330ft above the ground while an order pod is lowered on a tether.

The retailer noted that 90% of the US population lives within ten miles of one of its stores, offering an established network to support the expansion.

Walmart e-commerce fulfilment transformation senior vice-president Greg Cathey said: "Walmart's stores put us close to the communities we serve. With Zipline, we can build on that proximity and bring this fast delivery option to even more customers across the country."

The aerial service is part of Walmart's wider same-day fulfilment options, which also include delivery in 30 minutes or less in selected markets, express delivery within one hour, on-demand dispatch in as little as three hours, and scheduled delivery windows.

Zipline CEO and co-founder Keller Cliffton said: "Today, customers order from us multiple times a day. When you can get what you need in 10-30 minutes, it takes a huge amount of anxiety out of life. People can plan their lives around their loved ones, not errands."

The logistics expansion follows other recent operational updates.

Last month, Walmart introduced tools consisting of Agent Profiles and the Walmart Agent Gateway, applicable to both Walmart and its Sam's Club subsidiary, allowing authorised artificial intelligence agents to conduct customer transactions subject to designated expenditure limits.

"Walmart expands drone delivery with 300 Zipline locations" was originally created and published by Retail Insight Network, a GlobalData owned brand.
